# 13. Vehicle Integration Interfaces

An O-CPS implementation lives inside a modern vehicle architecture that is already dense with standards. This section specifies how O-CPS integrates without displacing the vehicle’s existing safety and security mechanisms.

## 13.1 Placement in the Vehicle E/E Architecture

O-CPS SHOULD be implemented in a dedicated V2X module or in a high-compute zone controller with physical isolation from the safety-critical powertrain and chassis domains. The V2X module MUST NOT have direct write access to any domain carrying ASIL D signals. All advisory outputs from O-CPS MUST pass through the vehicle’s existing ADAS domain controller, which retains authority for actuation decisions.

## 13.2 In-Vehicle Communication

The V2X module exchanges data with other domains through the following standardized interfaces:

| **Interface** | **Purpose** | **Standard** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SOME/IP Service Discovery | Advertise and consume service endpoints across domains over automotive Ethernet. | ISO/SAE 22900 series; AUTOSAR |
| SecOC (Secure Onboard Communication) | Authenticate safety-relevant signals (e.g., V-CTRL advisories) between the V2X module and ADAS domain. | AUTOSAR SecOC |
| DoIP | Diagnostic access to the V2X module over Ethernet. | ISO 13400 |
| CAN FD | Legacy interfaces to non-Ethernet domains. | ISO 11898-1:2024 |
| 1000BASE-T1 | Physical layer for automotive Ethernet where available. | IEEE 802.3bp |

## 13.3 HSM Requirements

The V2X module MUST have access to a Hardware Security Module (HSM) that supports ECDSA P-256 signature generation and verification, secure key storage with anti-extraction, and the attestation operations required for §9.2. The HSM MUST be certified to at least FIPS 140-3 Level 2 or Common Criteria EAL 4+. Private keys MUST never leave the HSM in plaintext form.

## 13.4 Time Synchronization

Accurate time is foundational. The V2X module MUST maintain a local clock synchronized to UTC to within 10 ms, primarily via GNSS, with a secondary network-time source for GNSS-denied operation. Outbound timestamps use this clock. Inbound timestamps are checked against it: a message whose timestamp is more than 500 ms in the future or more than its stated lifetime in the past MUST be rejected.
